t: Judaism is the religion of the people of Israel, whose Hebrew Bible tells of one God who made a covenant with them and gave them the Torah, the law and teaching that guides Jewish life.

After the destruction of the Second Temple by Rome in 70 CE, the rabbis rebuilt Judaism around the synagogue, prayer and the study of the Torah and the Talmud, allowing it to survive in dispersion across the world.

Through the centuries of exile, persecution and the Holocaust, and with the founding of the State of Israel in 1948, it has remained the faith of about 15 million people and the root from which Christianity and Islam grew.
dyk: The Dead Sea Scrolls, found in caves near Qumran from 1947, include copies of books of the Hebrew Bible about a thousand years older than the oldest complete Hebrew manuscripts known before them.
ev: By the biblical account, David makes Jerusalem his capital and Solomon builds the First Temple
The Babylonians destroy Jerusalem and the First Temple and take many Judeans into exile
The Second Temple is completed in Jerusalem after the return from exile, by the traditional date
The Romans destroy Jerusalem and the Second Temple at the end of the Jewish revolt
Judah ha-Nasi compiles the Mishnah, the first great work of rabbinic law
The Babylonian Talmud reaches its final form
The Jews are expelled from Spain
The State of Israel is founded, three years after the end of the Holocaust

f.origin: The land of Israel (ancient Canaan), in the first millennium BCE
f.founder: Traced by tradition to Abraham and to Moses, through whom the Torah was given; shaped by the prophets and the rabbis
f.scriptures: The Hebrew Bible (Tanakh): the Torah, the Prophets and the Writings; the Mishnah and the Talmud
f.followers: About 15 million, most of them in Israel and the United States
